---
name: failed-inferinstance-vs-named-theorem
description: A failed inferInstance used as evidence a step is expensive measures the instance graph, not the proposition — mathlib registers bundled-structure facts without instances
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a failed `inferInstance` is the evidence that a step is expensive, check
whether the same proposition is a **named theorem about the same object** before
publishing the price.

AJC r6: `PicEtGaloisBridge.lean` measured `IsOpenImmersion (coverSelfSection T γ).left`
unsynthesizable (correctly, with a live `sorryAx` control) and concluded "the covering
property is not available from the étale-precoverage machinery for free, and closing
this row means building it". But `IsOpenImmersion (Sigma.ι g i)` also fails
`inferInstance` and **is** a theorem: `(sigmaOpenCover g).map_prop i`. That object is
exactly what the same file's own next step (`selfTensorSpecCoproduct`) produces, so the
failure would have been read as absence at the very place the route lands.

**Why:** mathlib deliberately omits instances that would loop, exposing the fact as a
field of a bundled structure (`Cover.map_prop`, `OpenCover`) instead. Synthesis failure
is a statement about the instance graph and never about the proposition.

**How to apply:** before pricing a step from a synthesis failure, search for the
proposition as a *theorem* — including as a projection of a bundled structure over the
same object. And split the price: here the topology half was one line
(`Cover.mem_grothendieckTopology` + `zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology`), only the
geometric half was owed. The instance-goal form of [[failing-exact-on-composite-goal]];
see also [[failing-inferinstance-is-not-absence]] for the theorem-not-instance case and
[[private-hides-a-declaration-from-search]] for the search-level analogue.
